title: observability: automate Prometheus/Grafana and log-shipping for Private installs
author: Maya Patel
description: Adds automated provisioning and lifecycle management for the observability stack in Private installs. This PR introduces a reusable Terraform module, Helm chart opinionated values, upgrade/rollback hooks, smoke e2e tests, and curated Grafana dashboards/Prometheus alert rules. Motivation: customers running Redwood Private often instrument Prometheus + Grafana + log shippers manually. This work makes observability a first-class part of the private installer so customers get consistent telemetry out-of-the-box, faster onboarding, and predictable alerting. The change set includes: 1) terraform/modules/observability: module to deploy kube-prometheus-stack (Prometheus operator), NodeExporters, and Alertmanager config with sensible defaults and inputs for network restrictions and KMS-backed secret handling; 2) helm/observability: opinionated values.yaml and templates for Prometheus scraping targets (redwood services), role-based access, and Grafana provisioning of dashboards + datasources (Loki/Prometheus); 3) log shipping: Fluent Bit daemonset manifests and a Terraform submodule to configure centralized Loki or S3-backed object store (configurable per customer); 4) installer hooks: upgrade and rollback scripts that migrate PrometheusRules and ensure Alertmanager silences are preserved across upgrades; 5) dashboards/alerts: curated dashboards for key SLOs (latency percentiles, GPU utilization, queue depth) and critical alerts (prometheus:InstanceDown, high_error_rate, low_kv_cache_hit_rate) with recommended runbooks; 6) tests: e2e smoke test that validates metrics ingestion, dashboard provisioning, and that alerts fire on synthetic failure. The description below covers usage, configuration knobs, security considerations, and rollout plan.

release_notes:
- Private installer: enable optional automated provisioning of Prometheus, Grafana, and log-shipping.
- Adds terraform module terraform/modules/observability and helm/observability chart values for private installs.
- Automatic upgrade hooks to preserve PrometheusRules and Alertmanager silences.
- New e2e smoke test and docs: docs/observability/private-install-notes.md and examples/private/observability-quickstart.md
usage_instructions: To enable the observability module in a Private install set module source in your root terraform and pass: observability_enabled = true, grafana_admin_secret = <KMS-encrypted-secret> (see README). For air-gapped installs pre-seed the helm chart tarball and set helm_local_chart = true. Helm values can disable components: fluent_bit.enabled=false or grafana.provisionDashboards=false. The installer supports rollbacks: run installer/rollback_hooks/observability-rollback.sh which will automatically revert ConfigMaps created by provisioning and re-apply previous Alertmanager silence state.
security_considerations: Secrets are expected to be stored in the customers KMS and only wrapped tokens are stored in Terraform state via remote backend. Grafana provisioning uses read-only API keys for dashboards by default; write keys must be configured explicitly. Network egress requirements and RBAC required permissions are documented in terraform/modules/observability/README.md. We do not ship credentials to external SaaS; all endpoints are configurable and default to in-cluster Loki/Prometheus.
rollback_plan: Rollback is supported via installer rollback hook which restores the previous Helm release and re-applies preserved Alertmanager silence state. For major operator schema changes follow the documented upgrade matrix; the hook will refuse automated migration if an incompatible CRD version is detected and surface instructions for a manual migration.
testing_strategy: Unit tests for terraform modules and helm template rendering. CI includes a dedicated observability-smoke job that deploys the stack into a short-lived cluster, emits synthetic metrics/logs, and asserts that metrics ingest, dashboards exist, and at least one alert fires on synthetic failure. Added polling with exponential backoff to reduce flakiness.
notes: This PR intentionally leaves advanced Grafana datasource multi-tenancy for a follow-up (ENG-2201). The current implementation provisions tenant-scoped dashboards for the cluster-level observability use-case and is sufficient for initial Private customers.
